overview: This bill swaps control of federal land in Harpers Ferry, West Virginia, between two agencies. About 25 acres now in Harpers Ferry National Historical Park would move from the Interior Department to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) for its Advanced Training Center and would be removed from the park's boundary. In return, three parcels totaling about 71.5 acres would move from CBP to the Interior Department and become part of the park. No money would change hands, CBP would pay for a survey, and if CBP no longer needs its land for the training center, that land would go back to the park. As of May 4, 2026, it had passed the Senate and was being held at the desk in the House.
for: Supporters say the exchange lets the training center meet its needs while adding significantly more land to the national historical park, at no cost to taxpayers.
against: Critics say removing land from a national park for a law enforcement facility sets a precedent and could affect the park's historic setting.
